articles.title: Trump says he’s inclined to strike Iran after new year if no deal reached
articles.summary: President Trump said he was inclined to resume strikes against Iran after the New Year if no deal is reached between Washington and Tehran to end the conflict. Trump acknowledged that indirect talks between the two nations were still ongoing but described Iranian officials as “professional tap dancers.” He also accused the regime of stalling…
articles.body:
President Trump said he was inclined to resume strikes against Iran after the New Year if no deal is reached between Washington and Tehran to end the conflict.

Trump acknowledged that indirect talks between the two nations were still ongoing but described Iranian officials as “professional tap dancers.”

He also accused the regime of stalling negotiations, telling Fox News in a statement that “they talk all the time.”

“All they do is talk, but it’s all bulls—,” the president continued. “They’re more aggressive now than before the election.”

Trump said he hoped Iran would test the limits of the U.S. military’s naval blockade of nearby ports because if they did, “they’ll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy.”

This comes after Iran’s Foreign ​Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei told reporters at a weekly press conference that Iran would “use all our tools ​to confront this U.S. aggression,” according to a translation by Reuters .

“We will definitely not tolerate ⁠it [the blockade] and we will use all our tools ​to confront this US aggression,” Baghaei said. “The naval blockade…is ​considered a military aggression.”

In the past week, Iran and the U.S. have engaged in tit-for-tat attacks as both countries face pressure domestically to end the conflict. The Iranian strikes targeted a U.S. air base in Kuwait, while American forces struck Tehran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday following an unofficial quiet period of roughly two months.

Senate Republicans were able to defeat a resolution that would have directed Trump to end hostilities in the Middle East, though the GOP is set to lose its majority vote in the New Year.

Iran is similarly struggling to maintain its war effort as it faces difficulties financing its attacks due to the economic weight of the U.S. blockade.

articles.title: Bomb alert: Hyderabad cyber crime cops dismiss email threat as hoax, find sender used ‘disposable’ mail ID
articles.summary: Hyderabad cyber crime police dismissed a bomb threat email as a hoax after tracing it to a disposable mail ID; case filed under IT Act and BNS sections.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Anonymous miscreants who sent a bomb threat email threatening to target a hotel and railway station in Kachiguda have used a ‘disposable mail ID’ (a temporary anonymous email address with a predetermined lifetime that does not require any registration) to cover their tracks. A suo motu case was registered by Hyderabad Cyber Crime police on Sunday regarding the bomb threat, which turned out to be a hoax.The mail was sent to Hyderabad police commissioner’s official email on Saturday night by an unidentified person from the email address hayforago@addrin.uk. The sender had threatened to trigger bomb blasts at a hotel and the Kacheguda Railway Station.According to police, the email, titled Lashkar-e-Taiba, landed at cp-hyderabad@tspolice.gov.in at 7:13pm on Nov 21 from the address hayforago@addrin.uk.The sender claimed links to the proscribed terror outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba. “The email said the group’s leader and commander, Lateef Bhat, and several other leaders had been killed by the Indian Army and threatened revenge against govt through 26/11 Mumbai like attacks in Hyderabad which might cause a loss of 300 lives,” a police officer said.Following the mail, anti-sabotage checks were conducted at the hotel and the railway station by the bomb disposal squad and surveillance has been stepped up at both the places. Security has been stepped up at railway stations and crowded places.“The sender has used disposable email service which doesn’t require any registration to send an email to conceal his identity. In such cases, offenders also use VPNs and make it difficult to trace the original IP,” a cyber crime officer said.City police issued a statement on Sunday calling the threat a hoax. A case was registered under Section 66-D of the Information Technology Act and Sections 351(3) (Aggravated criminal intimidation), 351(4) (Criminal intimidation by anonymous communication) and 353(2) (Statements conducing to public mischief) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: ADAM KRAUT: The Supreme Court must defend the Second Amendment in key case
articles.summary: The Second Amendment Foundation argues Supreme Court cases on Dec. 2 will decide if the government can ban the AR-15, America's most popular rifle.
articles.body: While many Americans are still wondering what the results of the midterm elections will mean for their day-to-day lives, the Supreme Court is preparing to hear oral arguments for two cases that could impact millions of law-abiding gun owners around the country immediately. If you own a gun, or care about the Second Amendment, these cases are about you. On Dec. 2, the Supreme Court will hear oral arguments in Viramontes v. Cook County and Grant v. Higgins. Both cases before the Court challenge laws that ban so-called "assault weapons," a political label for semiautomatic rifles. It’s a scare-term designed to obscure reality and make ordinary rifles sound fringe and scary. Both laws before the Court ban the AR-15 by name and outlaw similar semiautomatic rifles based on features like an adjustable stock, a pistol grip, or a flash suppressor. These laws are unconstitutional and unfairly target law-abiding Americans. The Second Amendment Foundation has been in this fight since 2019, having filed 9 cases challenging these exact types of laws across the nation. As a plaintiff in both cases before the Supreme Court, SAF has stuck with these cases while lower courts rubber-stamped both bans. And despite years of slow and expensive litigation, the nation’s highest court will finally hear argument. SECOND AMENDMENT FIGHT MOVES BEYOND GUNS WITH SUPREME COURT POISED FOR BIG RULING The question before the Supreme Court is whether the Second and Fourteenth Amendments guarantee the right to possess AR-15 platform and similar semiautomatic rifles. Or, in other words, can the government ban the most popular rifle in America? We strongly believe the Constitution does protect Americans’ rights to own an AR-15 and other similar rifles. And there’s precedent to back this up. The Supreme Court has said it protects arms in common use for all lawful purposes. Tens of millions of law-abiding Americans own AR-15-platform rifles. These are firearms in common use, and thus, they are protected by the Constitution. DOJ SUES DENVER OVER BAN ON ‘ASSAULT WEAPONS’ AS CITY'S DEM MAYOR SAYS IT 'WILL NOT BE BULLIED' Simply put, if states can ban the most common rifle in America, then the Second Amendment’s guarantee means very little in practice. articles.title: Govt refunded Rs 93 cr to 2.39L chit fund victims: CM
articles.summary: Odisha govt refunded Rs 93 crore to 2.39 lakh chit fund fraud victims in two years, CM Majhi told the assembly; efforts on to identify remaining depositors.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Over the past two years, Odisha govt has refunded Rs 93 crore to more than 2.39 lakh victims of chit fund fraud in the state, chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi informed the assembly on Monday.“Altogether, 2,39,461 chit fund depositors have received around Rs 93 crore since the BJP govt assumed office in June 2024. The govt has taken necessary steps to return the money deposited by investors who were cheated by various chit fund companies,” Majhi said in a written reply to a question from BJP’s Balasore MLA Manas Kumar Dutta.Majhi said the refund process is continuing and efforts are underway to identify the remaining genuine depositors. Ganjam emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the exercise, with 1,14,401 depositors receiving Rs 41.84 crore.According to govt sources, 2,79,109 victims were refunded around Rs 119 crore between 2014 and 2024 during the previous govt’s tenure.Compensation for chit fund victims was a key BJP electoral promise in the 2024 elections.Around 70 lakh people in Odisha were reportedly duped by about 450 Ponzi companies between 2010 and 2014. Following a Supreme Court directive in May 2014, the CBI took up investigations against 44 companies, including Kolkata-based Saradha Group and Odisha-based Seashore and Artha Tatwa groups. The 44 companies allegedly collected around Rs 4,600 crore from investors in the state.Ahead of the 2014 assembly and Lok Sabha elections, then BJD govt constituted a judicial commission and created a Rs 300-crore corpus fund to compensate affected small depositors.The commission, headed by Justice M M Das, identified a large number of small depositors who had lost Rs 10,000 or less. In its interim reports to the state govt, it recommended refunds for 4,97,844 small investors and identified more than 450 companies allegedly involved in the Ponzi scam. articles.title: Mass clean-up in Cornwall after heavy rain and flooding
articles.summary: Communities across Cornwall pull together to deal with floodwater which caused disruption.
articles.body:
Communities across Cornwall have been clearing up after heavy rain and flooding caused disruption.

The Met Office had issued a yellow weather warning for heavy rain for Sunday. Post-storm figures showed parts of the county saw about 50mm (2in) of rain over a 24-hour period - almost half the total expected for the whole of November.

Gweek was completed flooded in the early hours on Sunday, and members of the community got together to clear debris and unblock drains.

Resident Daniel Kemp said he woke up to go to work and found "the whole of the road flooded" and "people could not pass".

Kemp said it was one of worst floods he had seen in the village "without hideous weather".

He and a group of others "cleared the drains, brushed up and cleaned up, and got the place working again".

Reece Adams, manager of The Ship Inn, Wadebridge, said he was concerned after he opened the door and a "good couple of inches of water started to creep in", as "floods of water of came down the hill".

He said he grabbed a hoe and cleaned five or six drains which had become blocked with leaves and debris.

Despite some claims the drains should have been cleared by council workers prior to the rain, Adams said he believed there was "not a great deal that could have been done".

"There's a lot of trees and foliage around here and, with the winds and rain, they are always going to be brought down with it.

"It's an unfortunate mishap of so much leaves and debris into the drains at one time."

The BBC has contacted Cornwall Council for comment.
